judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is , the empty target of the 'Skip to main content' skip link: no href, no content, no tabindex, no box (bounds null). claimTrue: the snapshot's own role for it is generic, but its Chromium accessibility node has role link and no name, so the sentence holds of the capture (the screen-reader announcement is the rule's inference). The reason for the link role is a browser heuristic: I loaded the live page in headless Edge over CDP and found the same node exposed as link, name empty, with a single click listener registered by the TikTok analytics pixel (analytics.tiktok.com/i18n/pixel/.../main.*.js); Chromium turns an href-less anchor into a link when it has a mouse listener. In HTML semantics (HTML-AAM) an a without href has the generic role, and W3C's ACT rule c487ae (link has non-empty accessible name, mapped to 4.1.2) lists exactly this case, an a element without href, as inapplicable because it 'does not have the role of link'. The element is not a user interface component under WCAG's definition: it is not perceived as a control, cannot be focused or clicked (zero size), and the only 'function' is a third-party tracking listener. So it does not fail 4.1.2. captureDiffers: the live page has the same markup and the same exposure, so no difference touches the claim. False positive: the rule treats a browser heuristic role on a fragment target as a nameless control, a stricter reading than 4.1.2.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the course search text field in 'Find your course'. Its placeholder 'Search courses by name/keyword' is the only visible text telling sighted users what the field is for: its label 'Search keyword or course' has class off-screen. claimTrue: the crop and screenshot show mid-grey placeholder text on the white field. I checked the live page in headless Edge: getComputedStyle(input, '::placeholder') gives color rgb(144,144,144), opacity 1, 19.2px, weight 400, on background rgb(255,255,255), which computes to 3.19:1, as stated. elementFails: 19.2px (14.4pt) at weight 400 is not large text, so 4.5:1 applies; none of 1.4.3's exceptions fits (the field is active, the text is not decorative, hidden, part of a picture or a logotype). I looked for a reason placeholder text could be exempt: the ACT contrast rule only scopes DOM text nodes, but WCAG does not exempt placeholders, and W3C's own forms tutorial (Instructions) treats placeholder colour as subject to 'the minimum contrast requirement of WCAG'. No reason holds up. captureDiffers: the live markup and computed colours match the capture. True positive.
